column1: # Cairn v2 partition table — A/B OTA from the first commit.
# The v1 layout was huge_app.csv: a single app partition with no OTA slots at
# all. Retrofitting OTA later means reflashing every device over serial
# for a unit wired into a car's OBD port is exactly the kind of job you do not
# want to discover you need. So the slots exist from the start even though OTA
# itself is not switched on yet.
# Budget on 4 MB flash. App slots must be 0x10000-aligned for OTA.
# The chip on this unit is a 16 MB W25Q128
column2: so roughly 12 MB is left unused.

column1: # That is deliberate for now: the 1.69 MB slots hold the current image at under
# two thirds full
column2: and changing the configured flash size alters the bootloader

column1: # header — a boot-loop class of risk for no benefit this firmware can currently
# spend. Growing the slots later is a repartition
# routine; it is the absence of OTA slots that would have been unrecoverable.
#   0x009000  nvs       20 KB   boot_id
#   0x00e000  otadata    8 KB   which slot is active
#   0x010000  app0     1.69 MB  OTA slot A
#   0x1c0000  app1     1.69 MB  OTA slot B
#   0x370000  nvs_keys   4 KB   flash-encryption key (see the note below)
#   0x371000  errlog    64 KB   error and reboot-cause journal
#   0x381000  coredump  64 KB   panic dumps
column2: so a crash in a parked car is

column1: #                               diagnosable after the fact
# Total used: 0x391000 of 0x400000.
# nvs_keys is present but flash encryption is NOT enabled by default. Enabling
# it in release mode is irreversible and makes a mistake unrecoverable on a
# device that is already in a vehicle; it is a deliberate
# partition being here means turning it on later does not require repartitioning.
